newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi ready to offer resignation - papers.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi ready to offer resignation - papers.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi will offer to resign on Wednesday in exchange for a deal with the centre-right opposition on the deployment of a security force for Albania, newspapers reported.

The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) was due to vote on the Italian-led mission later on Wednesday, with Prodi looking for support from the opposition Freedom Alliance bloc after a hard-left political ally refused to back the operation.
The Freedom Alliance supports the Albania force but said on Tuesday it would not vote for the government motion and called on Prodi to accept its own resolution.
But the government coalition decided at a meeting late on Tuesday not to back the centre-right motion.

Newspapers reported that Prodi, well aware that Italy's international credibility is at stake over the mission, would call on the Freedom Alliance to vote for a joint motion which would allow the operation to swing into force.
In return, Prodi "would announce the intention to go to (President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro) and offer his mandate," La Stampa newspaper said.
Corriere della Sera newspaper said Prodi, who took office last May, would make the offer during an address to parliament.
The Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Giorgio Bogi, told reporters that Prodi would make "an important announcement" in parliament later on Wednesday.
Prodi's office said the prime minister was expected to address the lower house before the afternoon.
The government comfortably won a first vote on the Albanian mission on Tuesday in the upper Senate, where it has a clear majority and does not depend on the hard-left Communist Refoundation.
But Refoundation holds the balance of power in the lower house and is ideologically opposed to the involvement of Italian troops in foreign operations.

The Freedom Alliance was due to meet at 10.30 a.m. (0830 GMT) on Wednesday to discuss its stance. The debate in the Chamber is scheduled to begin at midday (1000 GMT) with a vote due around 08.00 p.m. (1800 GMT).

Italy is expected to contribute 2,500 troops to the Albanian operation, France 1,000, Greece 700, Turkey 500, Romania 400 and Spain 300. The multinational force is due to be led by Italy and is scheduled to be deployed next week.
